scores.tell: Barely any: the soft matte envelope, stacked photos and green radial rings match the real polaroid and mojito cards. The paper is only slightly too smooth and puffy.
The cauldron looks like glossy purple plastic, with blob highlights, swollen toy proportions and fat stubby legs. The plain lilac room corner is empty, and the hero sits low.
The binocular viewer has an invented face and glassy chrome lenses that reflect the city. The deep, busy skyline and terrace scene competes with the hero.
The stone table and stools look soft, like clay, with fat bevels. The hero is small inside a full park scene with trees and a path, busier and deeper than the real swing card.
The helmet has a huge glassy amber visor with a hard glint and a high-gloss white shell, close to the statue-glossy lesson. The flat pink and purple split behind it is plain.
The backpack is puffy and felt-like, a pillowy toy with no flat faces. The loud red-orange diamond background is as saturated as the hero.
The frontal door fills the card, and dense ivy leaves crowd the edges, so it has no breathing room. Otherwise it is close to the real window card.
Barely any: the satin red keyboard on a blue rayed pattern of notes and stars matches the real whistle and towel cards. The rainbow buttons add a few extra hues.
The full beach backdrop with sea, sky and grainy sand is deeper and brighter than the real cards. The lacquered shell, the wet sparkly cans and the invented cow-face logo also give it away.
Every drum part is shiny gold, chrome or glossy blue lacquer, with heavy highlights and dark rim contours. The theatrical spotlight podium and the cluttered kit crowd the card.
